title: Coherence of normalized shifted finite-line pullback around a square
statement: Let A be a commutative ring killed by N, and t a normalized ordinary finite twist transport [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. For any commuting square Xprime --g--> X, Xprime --qprime--> Yprime, X --q--> Y, Yprime --f--> Y, assume N is invertible on Y, Yprime and X. Put L_T=A_T(1)[2]. The canonical derived inverse-image square isomorphism at L_Y, followed by g-star of the normalized q comparison and then the g comparison, equals qprime-star of the f comparison followed by the qprime comparison. Neither positivity of N, finiteness of A, properness, cartesianness nor a projective-line presentation is required.

source.place: Both defining components commute with base change. The finite-line coefficient coherence underlying that assertion, also used in the presentation trace square.

proof.text: For N positive, identify the given normalized transport with the canonical finiteEtaleTwistPullbackData transport using ordinaryFiniteTwistTransport_unique. The roots inclusion and pure scalar root generators characterize its comparisons. The canonical transport composition law identifies the two sheaf-level comparison composites around any commuting square.

Pass this equality through the degree-zero derived embeddings and the canonical shift comparisons. Their composition identities give the exact inverse-image square. Transport it across leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory on the four edges, cancelling adjacent inverse isomorphisms and using naturality. This is precisely the square for ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback.

For N zero, invertibility of zero on Y implies Y is empty: a point would give a nontrivial stalk, whose germ homomorphism makes the global ring nontrivial, contradicting invertibility of zero. The map Xprime to Y then makes Xprime empty. Derived module objects on the empty scheme are zero, so the two arrows with common target L_Xprime agree. This handles the omitted zero case without positivity assumptions.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback_square
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (N : ℕ)
    (hA : (N : A) = 0) (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    {X X' Y Y' : Scheme.{u}} {q : X ⟶ Y} {q' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {g : X' ⟶ X} {f : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq g q' q f)
    (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) (hY' : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y', ⊤)))
    (hX : IsUnit (N : Γ(X, ⊤))) :
    (derivedSquareUpperStarIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) sq).hom.app
        ((ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA Y)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
      (ordinaryFinitePullback A g).map (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t q hY).hom ≫
      (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t g hX).hom =
    (ordinaryFinitePullback A q').map (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t f hY).hom ≫
      (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t q' hY').hom
